Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our updated Order Form (v4) with the MSA redline highlights we care most about. The key commercial point blocking approval right now is the limitation of liability — our procurement and risk team are asking for clarity on the following:

- Cap basis: liability capped at fees paid in the prior 12 months (not aggregate over term).
- A proposed floor: greater of fees-paid(12m) OR $2,000,000.
- Exclusions from cap: IP infringement indemnity, breach of confidentiality (including data breaches), and willful misconduct.
- Consequential damages: excluded generally, but we want express protection for losses arising from data breaches and regulatory fines to be outside the cap.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on the cap metric (12 months vs aggregate), whether Redwood will accept the greater-of structure, and which carve-outs you can accept? We are aiming to finalize counterparty redlines by Feb 19 to get legal sign-off.

Looping you in — Acme wants a cap measured as fees paid in prior 12 months with a >$2M floor and broad carve-outs for confidentiality/data breach and IP. They explicitly want data-breach/regulatory fines to sit outside the cap.

Quick commercial take: we can be flexible but need to balance with insurance and risk. Proposed negotiation posture:

Option A (preferred legal/commercial balance): cap = greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months; or (ii) $5,000,000. Carve-outs limited to IP indemnity, willful misconduct, and third-party claims arising from gross negligence; confidentiality/data-breach remains capped but with separate sub-cap for regulatory fines.

Option B (if client insists): cap = fees paid in prior 12 months OR $2,000,000 (whichever is greater) but accept amplified carve-outs for breach of confidentiality/data protection and regulatory fines being excluded from the cap.

I've attached our initial redlines for the MSA focused on liability language and indemnities. Lauren — can you review the proposed Options A/B and provide suggested drafting (esp. how to present the sub-cap for regulatory fines)?

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - Liability cap and damages carve-outs

Marissa / team — reviewed. High-level legal notes and suggested drafting:

1) Metric (fees paid): A 12-month lookback is common and defensible. We should explicitly state whether \"fees paid\" means amounts invoiced and collected to avoid disputes.

2) Aggregate vs Annual: we should make the cap \"aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement\" unless Acme insists on an annual cap. Aggregate is better for us from a risk perspective. If we accept annual cap, tie it to \"amounts paid in the preceding 12 months.\"

3) Floor / multiple: market tends to be 1x-3x of prior 12 months. $5M is defensible for enterprise but may be a blocker. $2M floor is acceptable commercially if we narrow carve-outs.

4) Carve-outs: Recommend narrow, specific carve-outs outside the cap: (a) gross negligence/willful misconduct; (b) indemnities for third-party IP claims; (c) breach of confidentiality leading to unauthorized disclosure of Customer Data. For data/privacy-related regulatory fines, recommend allowing them to be outside the cap only to the extent they are legally required third-party fines/penalties and supported by evidence; otherwise carve them into a sub-cap (e.g., up to X).

Suggested language snippet (for negotiation):
\"Notwithstanding the foregoing, the limitation of liability shall not apply to (i) fees or amounts owed under Section X (payment obligations); (ii) indemnification obligations for intellectual property infringement; (iii) willful misconduct or gross negligence; and (iv) liabilities to the extent arising from breach of confidentiality obligations with respect to Customer Data. Regulatory fines and penalties shall be recoverable to the extent required by applicable law or as a direct consequence of a breach of Redwood's data security obligations, subject to documentation and mitigation obligations.

\"Limitation of liability shall be the greater of (a) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability; or (b) $3,000,000.\"

I can draft both a tight \"Option A\" and a concessionary \"Option B\" for Marissa to take into negotiation. Also recommend we gather the customer's insurance details (cyber/liability) before finalizing.

-Lauren
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acme.com>

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - Liability cap and damages carve-outs

Marissa — thanks for the quick internal review. A couple points from our side:

- Acme is not comfortable with a $5M floor. We are prepared to accept $2M as long as breach-of-confidentiality and data-breach losses (including regulatory fines and remediation costs) are outside the cap and survivable for the term.
- We are open to documentation and mitigation obligations but will not accept a sub-cap for regulatory fines — business and privacy teams require unlimited recovery for regulatory fines tied to Redwood's breach.
- Indemnity for IP remains uncapped and standard.

Can Redwood confirm whether indemnities for data subject claims (e.g., class actions) would also be excluded from the cap or be subject to the same carve-out? See attached revised Order Form for our edits.

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v4.pdf

Best,
Emily

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form - Liability cap and damages carve-outs

Emily / Jason — appreciate the clarity. Proposed path for negotiation (phone call recommended):

1) Redwood's opening: propose the greater of (i) fees paid in the preceding 12 months; or (ii) $3,000,000. Limit carve-outs to IP indemnity, willful misconduct, and payment obligations. For confidentiality/data-breach, propose an express exclusion for direct remediation costs and third-party regulatory fines tied to gross negligence or willful misconduct, but not unlimited automatic exclusion.

2) Concession: if Acme insists on unlimited regulatory fines outside the cap, we will ask for (a) higher floor ($4M) and (b) enhanced security commitments (SOC 2 Type II within 90 days or equivalent) and (c) cyber insurance confirmation.

3) Final fallback: accept Acme's proposed greater-of (fees-paid(12m) OR $2M) with a narrow paragraph that preserves Redwood's right to dispute causation and requires documentation/limitation of punitive-like fines.

Suggested next step: 30-minute call tomorrow (Feb 18) at 10:00 AM PT to align on a single redline. I will prepare draft Option A/B language for discussion (will circulate beforehand).

DocuSign / HubSpot refs attached.
